transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, um… I guess the main thing is my talking has been getting kind of mixed up. Not all the time, but enough that people tell me they can’t follow me.

I’ll start trying to explain one thing—like the keys—and then somehow I’m talking about jail, or a prayer rug, or chess pieces, and I know it makes sense in my head for a second, but it doesn’t come out right. I’m not trying to be difficult. I just… I thought maybe I should come in and talk to someone, if that’s okay.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy lately?

Yeah… I mean, sometimes I do feel kind of up. Not bad, exactly—like I’ve got a lot in me, like I can talk to anybody and I’ll laugh loud and feel… strong, I guess. Powerful maybe, but I don’t mean that in a weird way.

And, um… if somebody questions me when I’m like that, I can get irritated fast. Like I might snap or talk over them, even shout, over something small. I’m not proud of that. It just comes out before I can settle myself. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you’re feeling especially up like that, do you need much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I guess I do. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but when I’m like that I can sleep maybe two, three hours and then I’m up before dawn feeling… fine. Fresh, even.

Like I’ll start making plans for work or what needs cleaning, like sleep is something other people need and I don’t really have to bother with it. That’s probably not great, right?
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

Um… yeah, sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic or anything, but I have heard… like a man’s voice.

It’s usually when I’m at work, or around the building—like it’s coming from the vents, or the mop closet. It’ll say my name, or say I ruined everything. And it sounds real, like somebody’s standing right beside me.

I know that probably doesn’t sound good. I just… I’m trying to answer you right.
Have you heard that voice during times when you were not feeling especially up or energized?

Yeah… yes, I think so. Not every time, but there were calmer weeks where I wasn’t really all up and full of energy, and I wasn’t… you know, way down either.

I still heard him then. The man’s voice, like in the vents. And I still had that feeling—well, more than a feeling—that people in the building were signaling things about me. It went on for more than a couple weeks, I guess.

I don’t want to overstate it, but… yeah, it wasn’t only when I was energized.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I just gave up or anything, but there have been stretches where most days I’d wake up and just feel… heavy.

Like after morning prayer, I’d sit on the edge of the bed and just stay there a while. Empty, I guess. Like there wasn’t much point in cleaning myself up or going outside.

It’s hard to say it the right way, but yes… it has lasted longer than two weeks before.
Across the whole time you’ve been dealing with the voices and people signaling about you, have you been in either a clear manic state or a depressed state for most of that time?

I… yeah, I think most of the time it’s been when I’m more keyed up.

I don’t mean out of control, exactly, but I get going and I talk too much, and I start making these big cleaning plans that are probably more than I can really do. It feels like I have to keep moving, like I can’t slow myself down.

So… yes, if I’m answering it right, I’d say most of the time since all this started, I’ve been in those stretches more than the low ones.
Did these symptoms begin after you had a medical illness, head injury, seizure, or started using any drugs or new medicines?

I don’t think so, no… not that I can point to.

I mean, I haven’t had some big head injury or anything like that that I remember. And I’m not aware of seizures. As far as drugs or new medicines, I don’t think it started from anything like that.

If there’s a certain kind of illness or medicine you mean, you can ask me straight, but… I don’t think that’s how it began.
Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or feeling people were signaling about you while you were not manic and not depressed?

Yeah… I think there were times like that.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but there were some calmer weeks where I wasn’t really up like that, and I wasn’t down in that heavy way either. I was just kind of… normal enough, I guess.

But I still heard the man in the vents during that time. And I still felt like people in the building were signaling about me. That went on more than two weeks, I’m pretty sure.

Is that what you mean?
Did the voices and feeling that people were signaling about you come on very suddenly, within about two weeks?

I’m not really sure, doctor.

It didn’t feel like one day I was fine and then all of a sudden everything started within a week or two. But I also wasn’t keeping track that carefully, so I don’t want to give you the wrong answer.

I guess it felt more like it kind of built up, but… if there’s a specific way you want me to think about it, I can try.
Have the voices and the feeling that people were signaling about you lasted for at least one month?

Yes… yeah, it’s been more than a month.

I don’t like saying it like that, but the voices and that feeling like people were watching me or marking me somehow… that’s been around for maybe a year and a half now.

Some days it’s not as bad, so I try not to make a big thing of it, but it hasn’t really gone away. Is that the kind of time frame you mean?
Have you become much less interested in being around other people than you used to be?

Yeah… I guess I have, a lot more than I’d like to admit.

I used to do more with people. I liked taking pictures, playing chess, going to the mosque, even cooking extra food for neighbors sometimes. I wasn’t some social butterfly, but I had things I cared about.

Now… the camera just stays in the drawer. And when people call, I don’t always answer. I tell myself I’m just tired or busy, but really I just don’t feel like being around anybody much.

I don’t mean to sound bad. It’s just… yeah, I’m less interested than I used to be.
When you’re not feeling especially up or especially depressed, do you still find that your interest in people and activities is much lower than it used to be?

Yeah… even when I’m not really high or really down, it’s still there.

I mean, I try to tell myself I’m just getting older or tired from work, but it’s different than before. I used to like taking pictures, playing chess, going to the mosque, cooking extra for neighbors… normal things like that.

Now the camera just sits in the drawer, and if people call, a lot of times I don’t answer. I don’t want to seem rude or ungrateful. I just… don’t feel the pull to do those things like I used to. Is that what you mean?
Have these problems overall—the voices, the feeling people were signaling about you, and the changes in your thinking—been going on for at least six months?

Yes… yes, it’s been more than six months.

I guess if I’m being honest, it started after that brief detention, you know, the misunderstanding at the building. Since then it’s been… about two years and five months, something like that.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but overall, yeah, it’s been going on that long. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least one week when you felt unusually energized or powerful most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m bragging or anything, but there have been times where I felt really high, like… powerful, like I could handle anything.

It would go on for days, most of the day. I’d be laughing a lot, talking loud with everybody, feeling like people should listen to me. And usually I’d think I was just in a good mood, you know?

But if somebody questioned me or acted like I was wrong, I could snap. Like shout over something small. I’m not proud of that. But yes… I think there have been times like that, at least a week. Is that what you mean?
Because of these problems, have you become unable to keep up with your work or basic self-care compared with how you were before?

Yeah… I mean, I still try to manage, doctor. I don’t want it to sound like I just gave up.

But compared to before, yes. I’ve missed shifts, and I’ve lost some cleaning work because people said they couldn’t rely on me, or they didn’t understand what I was saying sometimes. That was hard to hear.

And outside work, I stopped going to the mosque as much, and I don’t really go to family gatherings like I used to. People invite me, but… I don’t always show up, or I leave things messy and unfinished.

There have been a couple times where it got bad enough that other people had to call for emergency help. I’m not proud of that. I’m just trying to answer you honestly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During one of those high-energy periods, were you ever hospitalized because of it?

I’m not sure I can say it was because of the high energy, exactly. I don’t want to answer it wrong.

There were times people got worried and emergency help got involved, but whether that counts as being hospitalized for that high period… I’m not sure. I don’t remember it that neatly, like, “this was for that.” Sorry, doctor. Is that okay to say?
At any time, have the voice and the feeling that people were signaling about you happened only when you were in one of those high-energy or depressed periods?

No… I don’t think it was only during those times.

I mean, I wish I could say it was just when I was really high or really down, because that would make more sense, maybe. But there were calmer weeks too, when I wasn’t especially energized and I wasn’t deeply depressed.

And even then… for more than a couple weeks, I still heard the man in the vents, and I still felt like people in the building were signaling about me. I know that sounds strange. I’m just trying to answer it the right way.
Have there been times when you heard the voice or felt people were signaling about you even though you were not feeling unusually high and not feeling depressed?

Yes… yes, there have been times like that.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but there were calmer weeks where I wasn’t really up or down like that. I was just more normal, I guess. And still, for more than two weeks, I could hear the man in the vents, and I still thought people in the building were signaling about me.

That’s what you’re asking, right?
During a time when you were not feeling unusually high and not feeling depressed, did the voice and the feeling that people were signaling about you continue for at least two weeks?

Yes… I think so. I mean, yes.

There were some calmer weeks where I wasn’t really high or depressed, at least not like the other times. And it still kept going for more than two weeks—the man in the vents, and feeling like people in the building were signaling about me.

I know that sounds bad, but I’m trying to answer it honestly.

doctor.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
doctor.question: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: What brings me here is my talking gets all mixed up—I try to explain about the keys, then the jail, then the prayer rug, then chess pieces, and people tell me they cannot follow what I am saying.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code.

patient.answer:
Well, um… I guess the main thing is my talking has been getting kind of mixed up. Not all the time, but enough that people tell me they can’t follow me.

I’ll start trying to explain one thing—like the keys—and then somehow I’m talking about jail, or a prayer rug, or chess pieces, and I know it makes sense in my head for a second, but it doesn’t come out right. I’m not trying to be difficult. I just… I thought maybe I should come in and talk to someone, if that’s okay.

inference.note: Added broad differential for formal thought disorder/disorganized speech: schizophrenia spectrum (paranoid/disorganized), acute psychosis, schizoaffective disorder, mood disorder with psychotic features, and organic psychosis. No evidence yet to distinguish among them.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a prominent elevated or unusually energetic mood suggestive of mania, which would help distinguish mood-related psychosis from primary psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy lately?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: There are times I feel so high and powerful that I laugh and talk loud with everyone, but if someone questions me I can snap and shout over a small thing.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling unusually high or euphoric, which directly corresponds to elevated or irritable mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, sometimes I do feel kind of up. Not bad, exactly—like I’ve got a lot in me, like I can talk to anybody and I’ll laugh loud and feel… strong, I guess. Powerful maybe, but I don’t mean that in a weird way.

And, um… if somebody questions me when I’m like that, I can get irritated fast. Like I might snap or talk over them, even shout, over something small. I’m not proud of that. It just comes out before I can settle myself. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the elevated/irritable mood episode includes decreased need for sleep, which would strongly support mania over primary psychotic disorders or brief psychosis.
doctor.question: When you’re feeling especially up like that, do you need much less sleep than usual?

target_item.name: Decreased_Sleep
target_item.manifestation: I can sleep two or three hours, get up before dawn feeling fresh, and start planning work like sleep is something other people need, not me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether during elevated periods I need much less sleep than usual.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I guess I do. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but when I’m like that I can sleep maybe two, three hours and then I’m up before dawn feeling… fine. Fresh, even.

Like I’ll start making plans for work or what needs cleaning, like sleep is something other people need and I don’t really have to bother with it. That’s probably not great, right?

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are psychotic symptoms, which best separates bipolar/manic-spectrum disorders from schizophrenia-spectrum and psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

target_item.name: Hallucinations

target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about hearing voices when no one else is present, which matches hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Um… yeah, sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic or anything, but I have heard… like a man’s voice.

It’s usually when I’m at work, or around the building—like it’s coming from the vents, or the mop closet. It’ll say my name, or say I ruined everything. And it sounds real, like somebody’s standing right beside me.

I know that probably doesn’t sound good. I just… I’m trying to answer you right.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms ever occur outside of elevated mood, which helps distinguish a mood disorder with psychotic features from schizoaffective disorder or schizophrenia-spectrum illness.
doctor.question: Have you heard that voice during times when you were not feeling especially up or energized?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There have been calmer weeks when I was not especially high or deeply depressed, but for more than two weeks I still heard the man in the vents and believed people in the building were signaling about me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the voice occurred during periods when the patient was not especially up or energized, which directly concerns psychotic symptoms occurring outside a mood episode.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yes, I think so. Not every time, but there were calmer weeks where I wasn’t really all up and full of energy, and I wasn’t… you know, way down either.

I still heard him then. The man’s voice, like in the vents. And I still had that feeling—well, more than a feeling—that people in the building were signaling things about me. It went on for more than a couple weeks, I guess.

I don’t want to overstate it, but… yeah, it wasn’t only when I was energized.

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, referential/persecutory ideas) occurring for >2 weeks outside clear mood episodes strongly supports schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.0), and argues against pure bipolar disorder with psychotic symptoms (F31.2) as primary. Disorganized schizophrenia (F20.1) is less supported than paranoid schizophrenia (F20.0) given prominent voices and persecutory/referential ideas rather than hebephrenic features. Depressive-type schizoaffective disorder (F25.1) and current manic episode with psychotic symptoms without broader bipolar course (F30.2) are less likely.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had a major depressive episode, which would support schizoaffective disorder over bipolar disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: On my bad days I sit on the edge of the bed after morning prayer feeling heavy and empty, like there is no point cleaning myself up or going outside.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a sustained period of depressed mood most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I just gave up or anything, but there have been stretches where most days I’d wake up and just feel… heavy.

Like after morning prayer, I’d sit on the edge of the bed and just stay there a while. Empty, I guess. Like there wasn’t much point in cleaning myself up or going outside.

It’s hard to say it the right way, but yes… it has lasted longer than two weeks before.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a major mood episode present for most of the total duration of the illness, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia and bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Across the whole time you’ve been dealing with the voices and people signaling about you, have you been in either a clear manic state or a depressed state for most of that time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: Most of the time since this started, I have been in those keyed-up stretches where I talk too much, take on impossible cleaning plans, and feel driven like I cannot slow down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether mood episodes, especially manic or depressed states, have been present for most of the overall illness duration alongside psychotic symptoms; this most directly matches the requirement about manic episodes occupying the majority of the illness course.

patient.answer:
I… yeah, I think most of the time it’s been when I’m more keyed up.

I don’t mean out of control, exactly, but I get going and I talk too much, and I start making these big cleaning plans that are probably more than I can really do. It feels like I have to keep moving, like I can’t slow myself down.

So… yes, if I’m answering it right, I’d say most of the time since all this started, I’ve been in those stretches more than the low ones.

doctor.intent: Assess for a medical or neurological cause of the psychosis to distinguish an organic psychotic disorder from primary schizophrenia-spectrum or bipolar-spectrum illness.
doctor.question: Did these symptoms begin after you had a medical illness, head injury, seizure, or started using any drugs or new medicines?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about possible medical, neurological, substance, or medication causes of the symptoms, but the provided symptom profile does not include an item covering substance/medication-induced or medical-condition-related causes.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, no… not that I can point to.

I mean, I haven’t had some big head injury or anything like that that I remember. And I’m not aware of seizures. As far as drugs or new medicines, I don’t think it started from anything like that.

If there’s a certain kind of illness or medicine you mean, you can ask me straight, but… I don’t think that’s how it began.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a period of psychosis lasting at least two weeks in the absence of any prominent mood episode, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or feeling people were signaling about you while you were not manic and not depressed?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There have been calmer weeks when I was not especially high or deeply depressed, but for more than two weeks I still heard the man in the vents and believed people in the building were signaling about me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether voices and signaling beliefs occurred for at least two weeks while not manic or depressed, which directly matches this requirement.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think there were times like that.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but there were some calmer weeks where I wasn’t really up like that, and I wasn’t down in that heavy way either. I was just kind of… normal enough, I guess.

But I still heard the man in the vents during that time. And I still felt like people in the building were signaling about me. That went on more than two weeks, I’m pretty sure.

Is that what you mean?

inference.note: Psychosis persists for >2 weeks outside mood episodes, and mood episodes are present for most of the illness, strongly favoring schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.0). Substance/medical cause is not supported by history. Other prior candidates are now less likely but not fully excluded from the candidate list.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the psychotic symptoms started abruptly to distinguish acute/transient psychosis from schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder with psychotic features, and schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Did the voices and feeling that people were signaling about you come on very suddenly, within about two weeks?

target_item.reason: The question asks about whether the psychotic symptoms began very suddenly within about two weeks, but the symptom profile only includes overall duration of psychotic symptoms and does not specify sudden onset.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure, doctor.

It didn’t feel like one day I was fine and then all of a sudden everything started within a week or two. But I also wasn’t keeping track that carefully, so I don’t want to give you the wrong answer.

I guess it felt more like it kind of built up, but… if there’s a specific way you want me to think about it, I can try.

inference.note: Gradual rather than sudden onset makes F23.0 less likely, but not definitively excluded from the candidate list on this turn. Presence of psychosis for >2 weeks outside mood episodes while mood episodes occupy most of the illness course continues to favor F25.0 over F31.2 and F20.0. No evidence added for F06.2.
